Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test testContainsIgnoreCase_LocaleIndependence checks the behavior of StringUtils.containsIgnoreCase with different locales. The test expects consistent behavior for case-insensitive contains across different locales, including Turkish ("tr") which has special case-mapping rules.

The current implementation of containsIgnoreCase calls String.toUpperCase() without specifying a locale:
```java
return contains(str.toUpperCase(), searchStr.toUpperCase());
```
This uses the platform default locale to perform the conversion. However, the default locale can vary, and for some locales such as Turkish, this can produce different uppercase mappings leading to inconsistent or incorrect results.

This matches the current bug report which points out that String.toUpperCase or toLowerCase() are locale-sensitive and using them with the default locale is usually unintended for case-insensitive comparisons.

The recent bug report with the highest similarity mentions adding methods in StringUtils that explicitly accept a Locale argument for case conversions, acknowledging that platform-dependent case transformations are problematic.

Thus, the root cause of the failure is that containsIgnoreCase uses locale-sensitive case conversion without an explicit, fixed locale. This causes the test to fail when the default locale changes for Turkish or other locales with special cases.

The fix would likely involve using a locale-independent case conversion (e.g., Locale.ENGLISH) when calling toUpperCase or toLowerCase inside containsIgnoreCase to ensure consistent case folding regardless of default locale settings. This aligns with the common bug referenced.

No other methods are directly involved based on available evidence. The issue is isolated to the case conversion in containsIgnoreCase.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
